abstract: To elucidate dynamic higher-order structures of RNA in human cells would be important not only to deeply understand the physiological functions of mRNA and non-coding RNA but also to establish precision medicine. tRNase ZL together with hook-type sgRNA works as a 4-base-recognizing RNA cutter. We thought that RNA structure probing using the RNA cutters with hook-type sgRNAs of various 4-base recognition sequences would provide valuable information on the higher-order structures of cellular RNA. In this study, we investigated the feasibility of this method in vitro. We examined nine 32-nt RNA targets of various degrees of folding for cleavability by human tRNase ZL guided by each of thirteen hook-type sgRNAs. The assays were carried out under four different conditions: at 37 or 50{degrees}C with MgCl2 or spermidine. From these assays, we identified four main findings: At least two consecutive G or C nt in the target RNA recognition sequence are needed for hook-type sgRNA to work as a guide for tRNase ZL. A longer target RNA recognition sequence of hook-type sgRNA provides better guiding ability, and the hook-type sgRNA that can form with target RNA a hairpin structure without bulged nucleotides shows a better guiding ability. tRNase ZL with hook-type sgRNA, which was designed to work as a 4-base-recognizing RNA cutter, can also work efficiently as a 3-base-recognizing RNA cutter in some cases. Cleavage of target RNA by tRNase ZL guided by hook-type sgRNA occurs only in unstructured or loosely-folded target RNA, suggesting that sgRNA-guided tRNase ZL can discriminate less folded regions from tightly folded ones in long cellular mRNA or non-coding RNA. Structure probing of cellular RNA by introducing into the cells the hook-type sgRNA designed based on the findings of this study would provide valuable information on the higher-order structures of the cellular RNA.
